sb_use_board_tip:
Play this part with the plug-in board
Selects the board's bank on this part. The built-in voice goes silent and the board sounds instead; the voice list and the editing area change to the board's.
sb_back_tip:
Back to the MU's built-in voices
Selects the voice this part had before the board (bank 0, program 1 if there was none). The board stays plugged in and goes silent.
sb_user_no_programs: This board has no programs yet. Put waves on it in the Sampling window (Make a wave > Your own board).
sb_note: The board makes this part's sound. The row above still works on it: volume, expression, pan and the reverb and chorus sends. The MU's own filter, EG, vibrato and part EQ belong to the built-in voices and do not reach the board, so they are not shown here.
sb_user_empty: There is no wave on this program number, so it is silent. Put one on in the Sampling window (Make a wave > Your own board), or pick another program on the left.
sb_env: Envelope (one key held for 1 second, then released)
sb_user_note: Attack is the rise, Decay the fall to the Sustain level while the key is held ("-" keeps the level), Release the fade after the key is let go. Changes are heard at once and saved to the board file. Waves are put on the board in the Sampling window (Make a wave > Your own board).
fce_set_tip:
Voice set
The 128 voices of the FC board, kept as one file in the "fcsets" folder of the settings folder. Each FC board has its own: PLG-1, PLG-2, PLG-3 and the 16-part board can each open a different set, or the same one. "(initial voices)" is the built-in set of 16; touching anything there makes a copy called FC SET for this board, and its voice list grows to 128.
fce_wave_tip:
Wave
Square: the lead and chord sound, its tone set by the duty below. Triangle: the 16-step bass wave; as on the real chip it has no volume, it sounds or it does not. Noise: hiss, snares, explosions. Metal noise: a short loop of noise, buzzing and metallic. The key sets how fast the noise runs.
fce_duty_len_tip:
Duty steps
How many duty settings the square wave cycles through. 1 keeps one tone; 2 to 4 switch between them for the shimmering, sweeping sounds.
fce_duty_tip:
Duty
How much of each cycle the square wave stays high. 1/2 is hollow and round, 1/4 brighter, 1/8 thin and nasal. 3/4 sounds like 1/4 on its own but differs inside a sequence.
fce_frames_tip:
Frames per step
How long each step lasts, in frames of 1/60 second. 1 is the fastest.
fce_tri_note: The triangle has no volume steps: these only decide when it stops.
fce_decay_tip:
Fade while held
While the key is down the volume drops one of its 16 steps every this many frames (1/60 second). 0 holds the volume. 4 is the plucked sound of the initial voices 9-16; 1 is a short blip.
fce_floor_tip:
Stops at step
The fade stops at this volume step and holds there while the key is down. 0 fades to silence. A soft key press that starts below this step does not fade.
fce_release_tip:
Fade after release
After the key is let go the volume drops this many steps every frame. 15 cuts at once, 2 is the initial voices, 1 leaves a short tail of a quarter second.
fce_arp_len_tip:
Arpeggio steps
One key plays up to four pitches in turn, fast enough to sound like a chord: the classic way to get harmony out of one channel. 1 turns it off.
fce_arp_tip:
Arpeggio step
Semitones above (or below) the key for this step. 0, +4, +7 is a major chord; 0, +3, +7 minor; 0, +12 the octave trill. Drag, or double-click to type.
fce_sweep_tip:
Starts off pitch
The note starts this many semitones above (or below) the key and slides to it. A high start falling fast is a kick drum or a tom on the triangle, a laser on the square; a low start rising is a jump.
fce_sweep_frames_tip:
Reaches pitch in
How many frames (1/60 second) the slide takes. It moves in steps, one per frame.
fce_vib_tip:
Vibrato
A vibrato this voice always has, on top of the one the modulation wheel adds. In cents (100 is a semitone each way), about 6 times a second.
fce_vib_delay_tip:
Vibrato starts after
How long a note is held straight before the vibrato comes in, in frames (60 is one second). Short notes stay clean; long ones sing.
fce_note: Everything moves in frames of 1/60 second and in 16 volume steps, as on the old game consoles. Velocity sets the starting volume, pitch bend moves up to 2 semitones, the modulation wheel adds vibrato. 8 notes at once.
fce_cc_tip:
Values moved by control change
The highlighted values are coming from the sequencer as control changes. They belong to the song, not to the voice set: a program change puts the set's values back. Moving one of them here takes it over from the control change and writes it into the set.
fce_cc_drop_tip:
Back to the set
Drops the values that came by control change, as a program change would. The voice set is not changed.
fce_cc_assign_tip:
Control change numbers
Every value of this editor can be moved from a sequencer with a control change; the number is shown beside each control. Here you choose which number moves which value. The numbers are shared by all FC boards and remembered in the settings.
fce_cc_assign_note: 0 leaves a value without a control change. A number can move one value only: choosing one that is in use takes it away from the other value. Numbers the board or the MU part already listens to are skipped (0, 1, 6, 7, 10, 11, 32, 38, 64, 91, 93, 94, 96-101, and 120 up). Values are the editor's numbers as they are; semitone offsets are sent with 64 as 0.
fme_set_tip:
Voice set
The 128 voices of the FM board, kept as one file in the "fmsets" folder of the settings folder. "(initial voices)" is the built-in set; touching anything there starts a new set from a copy of it. Changes are saved as you go.
fme_name_taken: That name is empty or already used by another set
fme_reset_tip:
Initial voice
Puts the built-in voice of this program number back.
fme_alg_tip:
Connection
How the four operators are wired. A filled box is an operator you hear; an outlined box modulates the one its line leads to (it changes the tone, not the level). The loop on operator 1 is its feedback.
fme_feedback_tip:
Feedback
Operator 1 modulating itself. A little turns its sine towards a sawtooth; a lot turns it to noise.
fme_drop_tip:
Pitch drop
The note starts this many semitones high and falls to pitch in about 30 ms: the thump of a tom or a kick, or a zap.
fme_noise_tip:
Noise
Random modulation added to the operators you hear: breath, hiss, the rattle of a snare.
fme_ratio_tip:
Ratio
This operator's frequency as a multiple of the note's. Whole numbers give harmonic tones; in-between values give the clang of bells and metal. Drag, or double-click to type.
fme_level_car_tip:
Level
How loud this operator is.
fme_level_mod_tip:
Level
How deeply this operator modulates: more gives a brighter, harsher tone. Harder key strikes add to it.
fme_decay_tip:
Decay
While the key is held, the time to fall to the Sustain level ("-" keeps the full level). On a modulator this makes the tone mellow as the note goes on.
fme_save_fail: Could not write the voice set file
fme_drum_note: This channel plays the FM board's drums. The drum sounds are fixed; pick a melodic voice on the left to edit its sound here.
hme_set_tip:
Voice set
The 128 voices of the harmonic board, kept as one file in the "harmsets" folder of the settings folder. "(initial voices)" is the built-in set; touching anything there starts a new set from a copy of it. Changes are saved as you go.
hme_frame_tip:
The four spectra of a voice
A voice has four pictures of its partials. A note starts at 1, moves to 2 and then to 3 while the key is held, and goes to 4 after the key is released. Pick the one to draw below.
hme_to_all_tip:
Same for all four
Copies the spectrum shown here to the other three, so the tone no longer changes while the note sounds.
hme_bars_tip_fmt:
Partial %d of 64
Drag across the bars to draw the spectrum: the height is the level of that partial (top = full, each line = 12 dB down, bottom = off). Partial 1 is the note's own pitch, 2 an octave above, 3 an octave and a fifth, and so on. The thin marks show the previous of the four spectra.
hme_t_peak_tip:
1 > 2 time
How long the tone takes to move from spectrum 1 (onset) to spectrum 2 (peak). Short for a struck or plucked sound, longer for brass that swells.
hme_t_sustain_tip:
2 > 3 time
How long the tone takes to move from spectrum 2 (peak) to spectrum 3 (held). A piano loses its high partials over a second or two; a pad can take several.
hme_release_tip:
Release
After the key is released, the time for the sound to die away. The tone moves to spectrum 4 over the same time.
hme_bright_tip:
Touch brightness
How much a soft key strike dulls the tone: the softer the note, the more the high partials are turned down. 0 gives the same tone at every strength. Controller 74 (Brightness) moves the same thing from a sequencer.
hme_inharm_tip:
Stretch
Pushes the partials above their exact multiples, the higher the more. 0 is an organ or a wind instrument; a little is a piano string; a lot is a bell or a metal bar.
hme_odd_even_tip:
Even / odd
To the left turns the even partials (2, 4, 6...) down: hollow, like a clarinet or a square wave. To the right turns the odd partials above the first down.
hme_morph_tip:
Morph partner
Another program of this set. Controller 71 (Harmonic Content) then slides this voice's four spectra towards that program's: 0 is this voice, 127 is the partner's partials with this voice's timing and volume.
hme_noise_tip:
Noise band
A strip of filtered noise added to the partials: the breath of a flute, the bow on a string, the knock of a hammer. Sine partials alone cannot make these.
hme_noise_center_tip:
Band centre
Where the noise sits, as a multiple of the note's pitch, so it follows the keys (8 = three octaves above the note).
hme_noise_decay_tip:
Noise fade-out
The time for the noise alone to die away after the note starts: a few milliseconds gives a click or a knock at the start. "-" keeps the noise for as long as the note sounds.
hme_listen_tip:
Listen to a WAV
Pick a recording of one note. Its pitch, the levels of its 64 partials at four moments, how far the partials are stretched and how its volume moves are measured, and this voice is replaced by the result. Only those numbers are kept, not the recording. It works for a single steady note; chords, noise and sliding pitches cannot be measured. Breath and knock noises are not copied (add a noise band by hand).
hme_listen_fail: Could not listen to that file:
hme_listen_done_fmt: Heard %s%d (%.1f Hz, %+.0f cents), %d partials, %.2f s, %s. Stretch %.2f.
hme_drum_note: This channel plays the harmonic board's drums. The drum sounds are fixed; pick a melodic voice on the left to edit its sound here.
